reading.title: At a new workshop
reading.text: Lina welcomes adults to a workshop. She says hello and adds “Nice to meet you” to someone she has not met before. At the morning session she says “Good morning” and asks, “How are you?” At the break, people ask for water with please and thank the server with thank you. A British guest informally says cheers. When someone thanks Lina for help, she replies, “You’re welcome.” A visitor says excuse me to attract her attention, then says sorry after dropping a pencil. At the afternoon break, “See you later” fits because they will meet again. At the end, guests say goodbye and take care. After an evening meal, good night is a farewell. Welcome is for arrival.

reading.title: Finding an agreement
reading.text: Two community groups want the same room. At the doorway, one member says after you. When she cannot hear a question, she asks pardon. A colleague moves a chair and says no problem; another replies to thanks with my pleasure. Someone says bless you after a sneeze. The room discussion includes an apology for an interruption. A neutral helper supports mediation. Through negotiation, the groups find a compromise: they meet at different times. Understanding and empathy help them consider each other’s difficulty. Their resolution brings peace to the discussion. Reconciliation develops later when they rebuild friendly relations. Forgiveness for a hurtful remark is a personal choice, not a condition of getting a room.
